review_cost.rationale: I'd approve with nits: split data.ts by page, extract a shared team composable, cancel the debounce timer on unmount, and type the API records. Nothing requires rework.

findings.issue: One 450-line module shapes the data for every page; all six routes import it, so any data-contract change funnels through a single file and every page's loading logic is coupled.
findings.suggestion: Split into per-page modules (data/home.ts, data/pokemon.ts, …) over a shared api/format core, keeping the existing section structure as file boundaries.

findings.issue: The 200 ms search debounce timer is stored in a signal but never cancelled on unmount; if the user navigates (e.g. clicks Next page) inside the debounce window, the pending callback fires afterwards and replaces the URL with /?q=…&page=1, overriding their navigation.
findings.suggestion: Cancel the timer in a cleanup (useTask$/useVisibleTask cleanup) or re-check loc.url in the callback before navigating.

findings.issue: The 'sync local team signal with the loader value' useTask$ is duplicated, with slight variations, in the pokemon and team routes.
findings.suggestion: Extract a useTeam() composable (parse/normalize/sync/cookie write) that both routes consume.

findings.issue: Module-level cache Map has no size cap or eviction on success; entries only leave on error/404. It is bounded by the fixed API snapshot in practice, but that's implicit.
findings.suggestion: Either document the bounded-dataset assumption next to the cache or add a simple LRU cap.

findings.issue: A non-404 upstream failure rejects the route loader, producing Qwik City's unbranded default 500 error page.
findings.suggestion: Add an error.tsx (or wrap fetchJson failures) to render an in-app error page consistent with the layout.

findings.issue: API responses are consumed through inline casts (`t.record.pokemon as {...}`, `pokemon.types` as any, `s.stat.name`), with no shared response interfaces.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the handful of API record shapes used (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type, Generation) next to the helpers that read them.

findings.issue: Two coexisting 404 mechanisms: per-route status(404)+null rendering for unknown resources, plus a [...catchall] onGet for unknown URLs. Both work, but the behavior is split across files.
findings.suggestion: Consider a single custom 404.tsx (or ev.error(404) thrown from loaders) so the not-found rendering lives in one place.

findings.issue: A single ~600-line global stylesheet with unscoped class names, rather than Qwik's favored scoped component styles.
findings.suggestion: Allowed by the spec and consistently organized, but moving card/section/badge styles into scoped style blocks would prevent collisions as the app grows.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic Qwik City app on the current stable 1.20 line: loaders own all data, heads resolve loader values, 404s use the documented status(404) pattern, and SSR state comes from cookies so nothing flashes. The cache layer and the team feature are both careful and clean, the latter fitting the existing conventions exactly. I'd approve with nits: split the god data module, extract a shared team composable, and cancel the search debounce timer on unmount.
